headline: Small investors are piling into AI stocks while big institutional investors turn defensive, according to market data.
score_reason: Market-positioning story from one outlet using two data sources; interesting but not a market event in itself.
importance_line: Individual investors buying the dip carry the most risk if AI shares keep falling, while the institutions stepping back could leave prices with less support, though one week of Citadel data and one strategist's reading do not show how long this will last.
summary: Business Insider reports that, according to Citadel Securities, a large US trading firm, individual investors bought a net $9.1 billion of US shares on its platform last week, the most in 15 weeks, including $2.6 billion of chip stocks and $700 million of neocloud stocks, the AI computing-rental firms such as CoreWeave, a record weekly amount for that group. Viraj Patel, global market strategist at Vanda Research, says institutional investors are moving into defensive shares and questions whether retail buying can offset their fading demand.
notes: Read in full on Business Insider.
